findings.summary: A content criterion containing a state phrase satisfies the check, so a file-only reading still passes.
findings.evidence: Path (a) accepts a reading when any criterion contains a state phrase, whatever its kind. A g6vy-shaped reading with the content criterion 'docs/explainer.md says the page is reachable at /explainer' contains 'reachable' and is accepted. A Grep can satisfy a content criterion, so the reading still only checks that a file exists. That is the misread the check is meant to catch, now in disguise. The plan rejects 'Require criterion kind behavior' because 'a behavior criterion that only says a file exists would pass'. That does not follow: requiring a behavior kind together with the state phrase is strictly tighter than the phrase alone. The behavior-evidence default asks for criteria that check the behavior happening. Fix: Require the state phrase to be in a criterion of kind behavior, or at least refuse when the only state-phrase criterion is of kind content. Add a test that refuses 'docs/explainer.md says the page is reachable' as a content criterion and accepts the same phrase as a behavior criterion. Update the corpus accepting cases and the edited governance tests to use behavior criteria. Check whether that triggers check_code_survey for code-class readings built by governed_reading/scoped_reading; if it does, put the criterion on a docs-class reading or supply the survey.
findings.location: Plan decision 4 and step 3 (acceptance path (a)); reading.rs governed_reading at line 7013 builds CriterionKind::Content

findings.summary: Technical nouns in OBJECT_WORDS will refuse ordinary code requests.
findings.evidence: OBJECT_WORDS includes crate(s), package, binary, image, app and artifact. In a Rust workspace these are common technical nouns, so technical verb uses would match: 'Share the parsing code between crates', 'Workers should share the package cache', 'Release the image buffer'. The plan's own risk list admits 'Release the page lock'. Precedent: the check_governance_coverage doc (reading.rs lines 3308-3310) records that the earlier word table was removed because it refused ordinary requests that used common words. Fix: Count crate/package/binary/image/app/artifact only when a destination word (npm, crates.io, docker, a registry) or a version token is also in the window, or drop them. Add accepting corpus cases for 'Share the parsing code between crates' and 'Release the image buffer before returning'.
findings.location: Plan approach 'Audience-visible object' and step 1 OBJECT_WORDS

findings.summary: The replay test's stand-in half cannot fail, and its fixed 'one recorded' assertion contradicts the plan's own fallback.
findings.evidence: Criterion 2 asks for a replay over the recorded request text of all three jobs. Grep of the snapshot finds only paraphrases of 7bf8 and 0wtc (docs/decisions.md lines 2105 and 4113); records/ is absent. The planner writes the two stand-in texts with no delivery verb, so the 'not caught' half cannot fail, as the plan admits. Step 7 also asserts 'exactly one entry is recorded' while saying the fixtures switch to recorded=true if the host supplies the texts. Those two statements contradict each other. Fix: Keep the user/host open question and resolve it before production. In the test, compute the measured count only over recorded entries. Keep the stand-ins as a separately labelled scope illustration with no 'measured' assertion. Make the recorded-count assertion follow the table, not a fixed 1.

findings.summary: D161 wording could trigger the decision-link parse.
findings.evidence: The decision-log parse finds supersession and amend phrases, and each one found needs a [[link]] entry. D161 is planned to mention D08 ('D08 and the governed paths are not touched'). Fix: Write D161 without 'supersedes', 'amends' or similar phrasing about D08 or other entries. Otherwise add the matching [[link]] (decision-links.toml is not a listed deliverable).
findings.location: Plan step 9 (D161 text); docs/decision-links.toml header lines 1-13

summary: Verdict: revise. I checked the plan against the snapshot by reading and grepping; I ran no tests. The plan follows the accepted reading closely and names real code: refusing_check (line 3225), check_governance_coverage (3313), has_phrase (3399), governed_reading (7013), replay_declaration (3986), and in the corpus base_reading, repo_files, run(), function_body and the step!(check_reading_references( anchor (line 801). D160 is the last decision entry. Grep of crates/ confirms the dependents list: the only tests with delivery-verb requests are the governance tests at reading.rs lines 7079-7257 and the corpus case at line 563, and the plan handles both. Placement after check_governance_coverage, the doc-order update and the narrowed 1-of-3 claim are sound. One major soundness gap: a criterion of any kind that contains 'reachable' or 'is served' satisfies the check. A content criterion such as 'docs/explainer.md says the page is reachable' therefore passes, which is the g6vy misread in disguise. The plan's reason for rejecting a behavior-kind requirement does not hold. Minor issues: technical nouns in the object list (crate, package, binary, image) will refuse ordinary code requests. In the replay test, the two stand-in texts cannot fail, and the fixed 'exactly one recorded' assertion contradicts the plan's own fallback if the host supplies the texts.
